work.title: #14000andCounting
work.brief: Raise awareness of children separated from their families at the US border.
work.did: Produced, filmed and built an art installation consisting of a 20 ft milk carton trimmed in white neon located in Venice Beach, Los Angeles with 14,000 individual milk cartons inside representing every child. Created and shared content live from the road, with daily photos and updates across social platforms.

Helped shape the team’s daily episodes, published on MTV’s network every day.

Drove audience engagement through views, likes, tweets and social conversation, which decided the team’s points.
work.result:
#NanoNorth won Season 3 with the highest digital engagement score, reaching 10M+ impressions.
Each of us won a car, a Tata Nano.

about.heading: Telling stories that matter
paragraphs: I started at a digital marketing agency, launching campaigns for Philips and fast-growing consumer brands. It taught me what makes people click, watch and share.

A master’s in New Media Storytelling at USC Annenberg took me to Los Angeles, where I produced immersive journalism for NPR, Al Jazeera, KCRW and Google, worked on advocacy campaigns at 72andSunny, and made a VR documentary that won a Webby Award.

Since 2019 I’ve been with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), starting in New Delhi and now in New York. I plan, write, shoot and edit campaigns on climate change, gender equality, poverty, crisis and digital transformation for audiences worldwide.
I work where strategy meets creativity. I write the brief, shape the idea, plan the distribution, make the film, and read the data that shows what worked.

offTheClock.heading: I’m also a travel creator
paragraphs: I make travel films and short videos. From the last post office in the world to the dunes of Namibia, the highlands of Atacama to the islands of Thailand, I look for places that wow me, people who inspire me and cultures that open my world. It energises me and keeps my short-form instincts sharp, tested on a real audience.
